issues.description: GKE detection by name prefix is a fragile, spoofable heuristic instead of using authoritative labels.
issues.detail: All three reviewers flagged `instance.name.startswith('gke-')` as wrong. Any VM can be named gke-* and bypass the check; the authoritative signal is the `goog-gke-node` label or managed-instance-group reference. Add an `is_gke_managed` field to the Instance ADT derived from labels/metadata in the service layer, and have the check consume that boolean.

issues.description: Metadata/PR description promise PASS/FAIL but implementation emits a third MANUAL state for GKE.
issues.detail: The check name, metadata.json, and PR description specify a two-valued postcondition, but the code introduces MANUAL for GKE instances. Either document MANUAL as part of the contract in metadata, or move GKE handling to a muted/allowlist convention. Spec and code must agree.

issues.description: Check name drifts between 'single' and 'multiple' across PR title, CheckID, folder, and CHANGELOG.
issues.detail: PR title and description describe detecting multiple NICs, but CheckID, directory, file, class name, and CHANGELOG all use `single_network_interface`. Pick one predicate name and align everything: CheckID, paths, class, metadata, and changelog. The artifact should be named for what it asserts.

issues.description: Zero-interface branch silently reports PASS, violating the 'single interface' postcondition.
issues.detail: When `interface_count == 0` the status stays PASS with an informational message saying the VM has no NICs. Zero is not one; it's a degenerate state that should surface as MANUAL/INFO or be explicitly asserted impossible per the GCP API. Don't default-through a contradictory case.

issues.description: NetworkInterface model drops the fields needed to distinguish a real cross-boundary bridge.
issues.detail: The NetworkInterface struct stores only name/network/subnetwork, discarding accessConfigs/natIP, alias IP ranges, and stack type. Meanwhile `public_ip` is computed in a parallel loop and stored on Instance. Move accessConfigs/natIP into NetworkInterface, derive `public_ip` from it, and the check can ask the real question with one source of truth.

issues.description: Metadata promises a network-appliance exemption via ip_forward but the check ignores it.
issues.detail: The Notes call out network virtual appliances as legitimate multi-NIC, and `ip_forward` already exists on the Instance model. Either honor it (MANUAL when `ip_forward=True` and multi-NIC) or drop the claim from metadata. A composable signal is sitting unused.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on one structural problem: the check's contract is muddled and its key heuristic is wrong-data. GKE detection by `name.startswith('gke-')` is spoofable and should be a derived `is_gke_managed` field sourced from the `goog-gke-node` label. Metadata promises PASS/FAIL but the code emits a third MANUAL state, and naming drifts between 'single' and 'multiple' across the PR title, CheckID, and CHANGELOG. Two secondary issues: the zero-NIC case silently PASSes despite contradicting the postcondition, and the NetworkInterface model drops the fields (accessConfigs/natIP, alias ranges) that would let the check ask the actually interesting question while duplicating `public_ip` logic. Verdict: useful check, sound data-structure direction, but ship-blocking inconsistencies in contract, naming, and the GKE exemption.
